name: Edo period
region: Japan; Edo, Kyoto, Osaka and regional contexts
summary: Urban commercial culture, theater, pleasure quarters, travel imagery, print culture and diverse ceramic/textile traditions; social class and occupation matter.

wardrobe.text: kimono and obi arrangements vary greatly by gender, class, occupation and century

hairstyle_headwear.text: elaborate coiffures vary sharply by role and era; never use one “Edo hairstyle” default

architecture.text: wooden urban architecture, shops, bridges, inns and domestic interiors

food_drink_tableware.text: ceramic/lacquer tableware and urban food culture

weapons_tools.text: swords for appropriate samurai status; avoid assigning them to every subject

transportation.text: walking, palanquin, horse and boats depending on context

writing_calligraphy.text: print labels/signage and calligraphy can appear; generated text should be verified

lighting_technology.text: lanterns and oil lamps for night interiors/streets

visual_arts.text: Hizen/Arita/Imari ceramic traditions for appropriate ceramic cases

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: Heian multilayer court dress used for ordinary Edo townswoman
modern school-uniform styling in strict reconstruction

prompt_fragments.ukiyoe: Use print logic rather than a digital cartoon filter: carved contour hierarchy, flat color areas, paper absorbency, registration, selective bokashi and composition built for the page.
prompt_fragments.ceramic: For Edo blue-and-white, use an Edo Japanese ceramic reference family rather than silently importing Ming Jingdezhen court motifs.

sources.supports: ukiyo-e collaborative production, cherry blocks, mulberry paper and multi-block color printing
Edo porcelain image showing retrospective Heian court-woman convention

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode should narrow city/region, decade, class/occupation and source family (print, garment, ceramic, architecture).
